sentences.en: Who has words to capture that night's disaster, tell that slaughter?
sentences.zh: 谁能用言辞描绘那一夜的灾难，诉说那场屠杀？

sentences.en: What tears could match our torments now?
sentences.zh: 什么样的泪水才能配得上我们如今的痛苦？

sentences.en: An ancient city is falling, a power that ruled for ages, now in ruins.
sentences.zh: 一座古老的城市正在沦陷，一个统治了数个世纪的强权，如今已成废墟。

sentences.en: Everywhere lie the motionless bodies of the dead, strewn in her streets, her homes and the gods' shrines.
sentences.zh: 到处都是死者僵硬的尸体，横陈在她的街道、她的家园以及神灵的神殿里。

sentences.en: All over now.
sentences.zh: 一切都结束了。

sentences.en: Devouring fire whipped by the winds goes churning into the rooftops, flames surging over them, scorching blasts raging up the sky.
sentences.zh: 被风助长的噬人烈火翻滚着扑向屋顶，火焰在其上方汹涌，炽热的气浪直冲云霄。

sentences.en: Treasure hauled from burning temples, the sacramental tables, bowls of solid gold, and the holy robes seized from every quarter, the enemy piling high the plunder, children
sentences.zh: 从焚毁的神庙中抢出的财宝、圣餐桌、纯金碗，以及从各处掠夺来的圣袍，敌人将战利品堆积如山，还有孩子们

sentences.en: and trembling mothers rounded up in a long endless line.
sentences.zh: 和颤抖的母亲们被驱赶成长长的、无尽的队伍。

sentences.en: So that was the greatest of all Roman poets, Virgil, and he was writing almost two centuries years after Hannibal's great war against the Romans, the subject of this epic series.
sentences.zh: 这便是所有罗马诗人中最伟大的维吉尔，他写作此诗的时间，大约在汉尼拔对罗马的伟大战争——也就是本系列史诗的主题——之后的近两个世纪。

sentences.en: And a century or so after the final defeat of one of the protagonists in this story, the
sentences.zh: 大约在这个故事中其中一位主角最终战败的一个世纪左右之后，

sentences.en: Mediterranean city of Carthage.
sentences.zh: 地中海城市迦太基。

sentences.en: And Tom, in that poem, The Aeneid, which is translated there by Robert Fagles, Virgil is taking us back, isn't he, to the legendary beginnings of Carthage.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，在这部由罗伯特·法格尔斯翻译的史诗《埃涅阿斯纪》中，维吉尔把我们带回了迦太基那传说中的起源，对吧？

sentences.en: So shrouded in myth, the story of its foundation by the Phoenician queen Dido.
sentences.zh: 这段历史被神话重重包裹，讲述的是由腓尼基女王狄多建立这座城市的故事。

sentences.en: And the colonists from Phoenicia are laboring to build the new city.
sentences.zh: 腓尼基来的殖民者们正辛勤劳作以建设新城。

sentences.en: They're raising the walls.
sentences.zh: 他们正在筑起城墙。

sentences.en: They're building the palaces and temples, the harbors that the Romans will later destroy.
sentences.zh: 他们正在建造宫殿、神庙，以及日后将被罗马人摧毁的港口。

sentences.en: And at this point, this bedraggled group of refugees who've been shipwrecked off the African coast turn up.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，这群衣衫褴褛、在非洲海岸遭遇海难的难民出现了。

sentences.en: And these people are Trojans.
sentences.zh: 而这些人是特洛伊人。

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 他们正是。

sentences.en: So they are, as you say, refugees from the sack of Troy by the Greeks.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他们正是特洛伊被希腊人攻陷后的难民。

sentences.en: And the man speaking the lines that you read so powerfully is their leader, a prince called
sentences.zh: 你刚才充满力量朗读的台词的说话者，正是他们的领袖，一位名叫

sentences.en: Aeneas, who is the son of Venus, the goddess of love and beauty.
sentences.zh: 埃涅阿斯的王子，他是爱与美之女神维纳斯的儿子。

sentences.en: And Aeneas in that passage is describing what it had been like to live through the destruction of Troy, to watch its topless towers consumed by fire.
sentences.zh: 在那段文字中，埃涅阿斯在描述经历特洛伊毁灭是怎样的感受，看着它那高耸入云的塔楼被大火吞噬。

sentences.en: And he is giving this account at a great feast that has been held in his honour by Dido because she has fallen in love with Aeneas.
sentences.zh: 他是在狄多为荣誉而为他举办的一场盛宴上讲述这段经历的，因为狄多已经爱上了埃涅阿斯。

sentences.en: And we talked about this in the very first episode that we did on Carthage, I mean, about
sentences.zh: 我们在关于迦太基的第一期节目中谈到过这个，我是说，大约在

sentences.en: 400 years ago.
Actually, I think it was episode 421.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我想那是第421期节目。

sentences.en: And people who listen to that may remember what happens next after this feast, because Aeneas and Dido go out hunting.
sentences.zh: 听过那期节目的人可能还记得这场盛宴之后发生了什么，因为埃涅阿斯和狄多外出打猎。

sentences.en: There's a storm.
sentences.zh: 天降风暴。

sentences.en: They take shelter in a cave.
sentences.zh: 他们在山洞里避雨。

sentences.en: And while they're in the cave, the earth moves.
sentences.zh: 当他们在山洞里时，地动山摇。

sentences.en: And Dido, although not Aeneas, assumes from this point on that they are now man and wife.
sentences.zh: 虽然埃涅阿斯不这么认为，但从这一刻起，狄多单方面认为他们已经是夫妻了。

sentences.en: The problem for Dido is that Aeneas has this destiny that has been plotted out for him by the gods, and specifically by Jupiter, the king of the gods.
sentences.zh: 对狄多来说，问题在于埃涅阿斯有着神灵为他规划好的命运，尤其是由众神之王朱庇特所安排的命运。

sentences.en: And this destiny is that Aeneas has to sail to Italy and found a town there that in due course will result in the founding of Rome.
sentences.zh: 这个命运就是，埃涅阿斯必须航行到意大利，并在那里建立一个城镇，该城镇日后将促成罗马的建立。

sentences.en: And so Jupiter sends Mercury, the messenger of the gods, down to Aeneas and says, you know, stop hanging around with this Carthaginian woman.
sentences.zh: 于是朱庇特派遣神使墨丘利来到埃涅阿斯身边，对他说，你知道的，别跟这个迦太基女人鬼混了。

sentences.en: Get on.
sentences.zh: 出发吧。

sentences.en: Go and found Rome.
sentences.zh: 去建立罗马。

sentences.en: And Aeneas is very obedient to the will of the gods.
sentences.zh: 埃涅阿斯对神意十分顺从。

sentences.en: And so he dumps Dido and he sails away from Carthage for Italy.
sentences.zh: 因此他抛弃了狄多，乘船离开迦太基前往意大利。

sentences.en: And Dido is so distraught at being portrayed like this that she stabs herself to death with
sentences.zh: 狄多对被如此对待感到无比绝望，于是她用

sentences.en: Aeneas's sword, but not before she has called for her descendants to nurture an undying hatred for the descendants of Aeneas.
sentences.zh: 埃涅阿斯的剑自刺身亡，但在死前，她呼吁自己的后代对埃涅阿斯的后代怀有不共戴天的仇恨。

sentences.en: Shore clash with shore, sea against sea and sword against sword.
sentences.zh: 海岸对撞海岸，海洋对撞海洋，刀剑对撞刀剑。

sentences.en: This is my curse.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的诅咒。

sentences.en: War between all our peoples, all their children.
sentences.zh: 愿我们所有人、所有的子孙后代之间爆发战争。

sentences.en: Endless war.
sentences.zh: 永无止境的战争。

sentences.en: That's her curse, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就是她的诅咒，对吧？

sentences.en: And that's how it all begins.
sentences.zh: 一切就是这样开始的。

sentences.en: So she summons a demon to rise up from her bones, an avenger still unknown, to stalk the descendants of Aeneas and to hunt them down with fire and iron.
sentences.zh: 于是她召唤一个恶魔从她的白骨中复苏，一个尚不为人知的复仇者，去纠缠埃涅阿斯的后代，用烈火与铁剑追杀他们。

sentences.en: And Tom, who is this demon?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这个恶魔是谁？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, every Roman reading the Aeneid when it came out in the age of Augustus knew exactly who was meant.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，奥古斯都时代每一个读到《埃涅阿斯纪》出版的罗马人都清楚指的是谁。

sentences.en: It was Hannibal, Hannibal Barker, that great military genius whose career we've been describing
sentences.zh: 那就是汉尼拔，巴卡的汉尼拔，那位伟大的军事天才，我们在

sentences.en: in our previous episodes, who for almost two decades had indeed fought the Romans with fire and iron.
sentences.zh: 之前的节目中描述过他的生平，他曾用烈火与铁剑与罗马人战斗了近二十年。

sentences.en: Now, Hannibal, as we heard in our last episode, ends up this hunted fugitive, this defeated fugitive, kills himself in 183 BC.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在上一期节目中所听到的，汉尼拔最终落得个被追捕的逃亡者、战败的逃亡者的下场，并于公元前183年自杀身亡。

sentences.en: But it's the measure of the shock he had given Rome and of the terror that he had inspired
sentences.zh: 但从他给罗马人带来的震撼程度，以及他在罗马人心中激起的恐惧来看，

sentences.en: in Roman hearts that still, more than a century and a half after his death, in the age of Augustus,
sentences.zh: 哪怕在他死后一个半世纪多之后的奥古斯都时代，

sentences.en: you know, when the Roman Empire stands splendid and without a conceivable rival on the face of the planet, Hannibal continues to haunt the memory of the Romans.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当罗马帝国傲立于世、光芒万丈且放眼全球难逢敌手之时，汉尼拔依然萦绕在罗马人的记忆中。

sentences.en: And so I think it's not hard to imagine what a bogeyman he must have seemed to Romans who had lived through his invasion of Italy and who were born in the generation or two after
sentences.zh: 所以我想不难想象，对于那些经历过他入侵意大利、且出生在他对罗马人发动大战后的一两代人当中的罗马人来说，他一定显得像个可怕的怪物。

sentences.en: the great war that he had prosecuted against the Romans.
sentences.zh: 他与罗马人进行了那场大战。

sentences.en: So that means that even though Carthage has been defeated and forced to accept a punitive
sentences.zh: 这意味着，尽管迦太基已经被击败并被迫接受了一项惩罚性的

sentences.en: peace deal, the memory of Hannibal and of Carthage's assault on Italy means that for the Romans, in the decades after victory, Carthage remains the supreme enemy.
sentences.zh: 和平协议，但汉尼拔以及迦太基对意大利的进攻的记忆意味着，对于胜利之后的数十年里的罗马人来说，迦太基依然是头号大敌。

sentences.en: You know, would I be going too far to say there's still a sense of unfinished business for the Romans?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果我说罗马人心中依然有一种未了的心愿，会不会太过分？

sentences.en: Completely, completely.
sentences.zh: 完全不会，完全不会。

sentences.en: Listeners may remember that in our previous series, we talked about
sentences.zh: 听众们可能还记得，在之前的系列节目中，我们谈到了

sentences.en: Hannibal's preparations for the invasion of Italy in 218.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔为公元前218年入侵意大利做出的准备。

sentences.en: And he has a dream.
sentences.zh: 他做了一个梦。

sentences.en: And in that dream, he sees a giant serpent that is following in his wake as he invades Italy.
sentences.zh: 在梦中，他看到一条巨蛇在自己入侵意大利的尾随之路上紧随其后。

sentences.en: And this serpent, quote, causing massive destruction to trees and bushes, a deafening thunderstorm following in its wake.
sentences.zh: 引文称，这条巨蛇“对树木和灌木造成了巨大的破坏，震耳欲聋的雷雨在其身后紧紧跟随”。

sentences.en: And a god then explains to him what this serpent is.
sentences.zh: 然后一位神明向他解释了这条蛇是什么。

sentences.en: This serpent is Hannibal himself.
sentences.zh: 这条蛇就是汉尼拔本人。

sentences.en: And so the dream is portending what the Romans called the vastatio Italiae, the destruction of Italy.
sentences.zh: 因此这个梦预示着罗马人所说的“意大利大破坏”（vastatio Italiae）。

sentences.en: And that is exactly what Hannibal had inflicted on Italy.
sentences.zh: 这正是汉尼拔对意大利造成的浩劫。

sentences.en: So monstrous casualty figures, hundreds of thousands of people dead.
sentences.zh: 极其惊人的伤亡数字，数十万人死亡。

sentences.en: Fields, vineyards, orchards going up in flames year after year after year.
sentences.zh: 田野、葡萄园、果园年复一年地在大火中化为灰烬。

sentences.en: And nothing like it had remotely been experienced by the Romans or the peoples of Italy.
sentences.zh: 罗马人或意大利各族人民从未经历过哪怕与之相似的事情。

sentences.en: You know, for two or three generations, there hadn't been anything like this.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，两三代人的时间里，都不曾有过这样的遭遇。

sentences.en: And today there is considerable debate among historians about how bad the damage inflicted by Hannibal on Italy actually was.
sentences.zh: 如今，历史学家们对于汉尼拔对意大利造成的破坏究竟有多严重，存在着相当大的争论。

sentences.en: So opinions range from completely apocalyptic to merely, you know, pretty devastating.
sentences.zh: 因此，大家的观点从彻底的世界末日般的毁灭，到仅仅是“相当具有毁灭性”不等。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But however bad it was, what mattered was that the Romans in the wake of Hannibal's war remembered it as complete devastation.
sentences.zh: 但无论破坏有多严重，重要的是，在汉尼拔战争结束后，罗马人将其铭记为彻底的毁灭。

sentences.en: So to quote
sentences.zh: 借用

sentences.en: Simon Hornblower on this, I mean, he's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 西蒙·霍恩布劳尔对此的看法，我的意思是，他是完全正确的。

sentences.en: The trauma of Hannibal's lengthy presence, however great or small, the actual damage he wrought will not have been easily forgotten.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔长期驻留所带来的创伤，无论他造成的实际破坏是大是小，都不会轻易被遗忘。

sentences.en: To that extent, Hannibal's dream may have been a true prophecy.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，汉尼拔的梦可能是一个真正的预言。

sentences.en: Perceptions are a kind of reality.
sentences.zh: 感知本身就是一种现实。

sentences.en: I mean, we know that throughout history.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，纵观历史我们都知道这一点。

sentences.en: And the Romans, I mean, the damage that the Carthaginians have inflicted is so deeply embedded in the Roman imagination.
sentences.zh: 而罗马人——我是说，迦太基人造成的破坏深深地烙印在罗马人的想象中。

sentences.en: So the Romans come to talk about the Carthaginians, they use these expressions, punica fides, punica fraus.
sentences.zh: 因此，当罗马人谈论迦太基人时，他们会使用这些词汇：背信弃义（punica fides）、迦太基欺诈（punica fraus）。

sentences.en: The idea that the
sentences.zh: 这种观念认为

sentences.en: Carthaginians are the embodiments, almost the linguistic embodiments of cruelty and deceit and
sentences.zh: 迦太基人是残酷、欺骗、

sentences.en: infidelity and fraud and all of these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 不忠、虚伪以及所有这类行为的化身，甚至可以说是语言上的化身。

sentences.en: And the Carthaginians come to assume this almost kind of demonic place in the Roman imagination.
sentences.zh: 在罗马人的想象中，迦太基人几乎占据了一种恶魔般的地位。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你想想英国人在第一次世界大战后、甚至更甚在第二次世界大战后是如何看待德国人的，罗马人看待迦太基人的方式也有几分类似，听过这个系列节目的朋友可能会

sentences.en: the way that the Romans view the Carthaginians and people who've listened to this series may well
sentences.zh: 觉得这有点五十步笑百步，因为罗马人自己也曾以残忍、欺诈、背叛等行为而闻名。

sentences.en: feel that this is a bit rich because the Romans as well have been known to display cruelty and deceit and treachery and so on.
sentences.zh: 但这其实并不重要，因为罗马人的感受就是他们的真实感受。

sentences.en: But that doesn't really matter because the Romans felt what they felt.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是对迦太基人普遍的厌恶，更是某种更深的东西——一种最终近乎盲目的长久恐惧。

sentences.en: And this wasn't just a kind of widespread loathing of the Carthaginians, but something more, a kind of biding fear that was ultimately irrational.
sentences.zh: 之所以盲目，是因为迦太基人已经被彻底击败了。

sentences.en: Well, irrational because the Carthaginians have been completely beaten.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，被彻底粉碎了。

sentences.en: You know, completely smashed.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的是，迦太基作为大国的日子已经彻底结束了，因为罗马人在击败汉尼拔后

sentences.en: It is so clear that, you know, the days of Carthage as a great power are finished because the terms that the Romans had imposed on Carthage in the wake of
sentences.zh: 强加给迦太基的条款，旨在使其永远瘫痪。

sentences.zh: 为了提醒听众这些条款是什么：一项毁灭性的赔款，分50年期分期支付，旨在扼杀迦太基的经济。

sentences.en: So just to remind listeners of what those terms were, a devastating indemnity payable in installments over the course of 50 years designed to kneecap Carthage's economy.
sentences.zh: 丧失其所有的海外领地。

sentences.en: The loss of all her overseas territories.
sentences.zh: 迦太基曾统治过一个伟大的帝国，西西里、西班牙等等，全部失去了。

sentences.zh: 他不断地蚕食迦太基的腹地。

sentences.zh: 比如，北非的橄榄林等等。

sentences.zh: 而且那里不断发生各种边界争端之类的事情。

sentences.en: And certainly they were kind of very legalistic.
sentences.zh: 所以即使他们在攻击马其顿国王或扣押希腊显贵作为人质时，他们也总是需要觉得自己这样做在法律上是正当的。

sentences.en: So even when they are attacking Macedonian kings or taking Greek bigwigs hostage, they always needed to feel that they were legally justified in what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，他们没有做任何不合情理或无端挑衅的事。

sentences.en: They're not, as they see it, doing anything that is unmerited or unprovoked.
sentences.zh: 他们总是必须觉得神明是站在他们这一边的。

sentences.en: They always have to feel that the gods are on their side.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是元老院中大批人对迦太基的态度。

sentences.en: And so this is what large numbers in the Senate feel they need with regard to Carthage.
sentences.zh: 没有开战理由，他们就无法攻击迦太基。

sentences.en: They can't attack Carthage without a casus belli.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，他们手头正好有一个，因为这个人就是马西尼萨。

sentences.en: And fortunately for them, they have one on hand because this is Masinissa.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 所以这家伙一直跟迦太基人发生边境冲突，攻击他们的农田，抢夺他们的橄榄园什么的。

sentences.en: So this bloke has been constantly having his border skirmishes with the Carthaginians and attacking their farmland and snatching their, you know, their olive groves or whatever.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是加图或罗马的主战派，这不正是绝佳的机会吗？

sentences.en: But if you're Cato or one of the war hawks in Rome, isn't this the perfect opportunity?
sentences.zh: 他就像是乌克兰东部顿涅茨克和卢甘斯克的那些人的翻版，弗拉基米尔·普京基本上把这些人当成了他在乌克兰发动战争的借口。

sentences.en: He's like the equivalent of the people in Donetsk and Luhansk in eastern Ukraine who Vladimir Putin used as a pretext basically for his war in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 因此，此时已经八十多岁的马西尼萨依然如以往一样贪婪。

sentences.en: And so Masinissa by now in his late 80s is as acquisitive as ever.
sentences.zh: 所以他的部下继续对迦太基乡村腹地的农场和庄园发动袭击，目的是将其据为己有。

sentences.en: And so his men continue to launch attacks on farms and estates in Carthage's rural hinterland with the aim of appropriating them.
sentences.zh: 而在迦太基，人们现在感到绝望，认为罗马绝不会约束马西尼萨。

sentences.en: And in Carthage, there is now total despair that Rome will ever reign Masinissa in.
sentences.zh: 这种绝望将比前一代人更为好战的新领导人推上了权力宝座。

sentences.en: And this despair brings new leaders to power who are much more hawkish than the previous generation.
sentences.zh: 这些人说，瞧，我们需要更强硬的外交政策。

sentences.en: And these are men who are saying, well, look, we need a more assertive foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 我们，你知道的，我们不能再这样下去了。

sentences.en: We, you know, we cannot go on like this.
sentences.zh: 所以在公元前151年，迦太基人无视他们在公元前201年与罗马签定的条约规定，对马西尼萨开战了。

sentences.en: So in 151, ignoring the prescriptions of the treaty that they had signed with Rome back in 201, the Carthaginians go to war with Masinissa.
sentences.zh: 他们没有获得罗马人的许可。

sentences.en: They do not have the permission of the Romans to do this.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，对于迦太基人来说，结果是一场灾难。

sentences.en: And the result for the Carthaginians, unfortunately, is disaster.
sentences.zh: 所以马西尼萨，他基本上已经90岁了，但依然鞍马劳顿。

sentences.en: So Masinissa, he's he's he's now basically 90, but he's still in the saddle.
sentences.zh: 他在一个叫奥雷斯科帕的小镇附近与迦太基军队激战，双方势均力敌，他将迦太基军队困在了一座山上。

sentences.en: He fights the Carthaginian army to a standstill near a town called Orescoppa, and he isolates them on a hill.
sentences.zh: 他们没有任何水源，因此别无选择，只能投降并接受屈辱的条款，其中同样包括巨额赔款。

sentences.en: They don't have any water, so they have no option but to surrender and submit to humiliating terms, which include, again, a kind of massive indemnity.
sentences.zh: 这已经够糟糕了。

sentences.en: Which is bad enough.
sentences.zh: 但真正的灾难是，迦太基人显然给罗马的主战派送上了一份大礼，

sentences.en: But the real disaster is the open goal, obviously, that the Carthaginians have now given to the war party in Rome,
sentences.zh: 因为那里的主战派现在可以辩称，迦太基违反了条约义务。

sentences.en: because hawks there can now argue that Carthage is in breach of her treaty obligations.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果罗马攻击迦太基，神明将会支持他们。

sentences.en: And that, therefore, if the Romans attack Carthage, the gods will be backing them.
sentences.zh: 所以这正是他们所需要的一切。

sentences.en: So that's everything they need.
sentences.zh: 现在罗马人有了发动进攻的机会。

sentences.en: So now the Romans have their opportunity to launch their strike.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，还有经济动机，对吧？

sentences.en: And what is more, there are financial motives, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 因为在公元前151年，迦太基人刚刚付清了他们的战争赔款的最后一笔分期付款。

sentences.en: Because in 151, the Carthaginians have paid off the very last installment, basically, of their reparations, their war indemnity.
sentences.zh: 所以以后再也不会有资金从迦太基流入罗马了。

sentences.en: So there's going to be no more money coming to Rome from Carthage.
sentences.zh: 如果罗马人想要迦太基的财富，他们就必须亲自去夺取。

sentences.en: If the Romans want the Carthaginian wealth, they have to go and seize it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们既有借由马西尼萨事件带来的外交机遇，

sentences.en: So they've both got the kind of diplomatic opportunity because this business with Massinissa,
sentences.zh: 同时现在罗马那些贪婪之人也有了巨大的经济诱因去鼓动对迦太基的战争。

sentences.en: but also now there is a very big financial incentive for greedy people in Rome to urge a war with Carthage.
sentences.zh: 这就像那些人说的那样，好吧，这就像是，我不知道，萨达姆·侯赛因是个坏人，伊拉克有大量的石油。

sentences.en: It's like these people who say, well, it's like, I don't know, Saddam Hussein is a bad man and there's a lot of oil in Iraq.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们上吧。

sentences.en: You know, let's go in.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 所以在公元前150年，罗马人开始动员入侵非洲。

sentences.en: And so in 150, the Romans begin to mobilize for an invasion of Africa.
sentences.zh: 而在迦太基，可以想见，这个消息让整座城市陷入了恐慌。

sentences.en: And back in Carthage, understandably, the news of this throws the entire city into panic.
sentences.zh: 于是他们拼命试图安抚罗马人。

sentences.en: And so they desperately try to appease the Romans.
sentences.zh: 他们首先通过将那个在奥雷斯科帕战败的将军判处死刑来做到这一点。

sentences.en: And they do this, first of all, by condemning the general who'd been defeated at Oroscopa to death.
sentences.zh: 听过本系列节目的老听众一定不会奇怪，这位将军的名字当然叫哈斯德鲁巴。

sentences.en: And it will not surprise regular listeners to this series to learn that the name of this general is, of course, Hasdrapal.
sentences.zh: 又一个，又一个哈斯德鲁巴。

sentences.en: Yet another, yet another Hasdrapal.
sentences.zh: 然后迦太基人向罗马派遣了一个使团，基本上是去乞求宽恕。

sentences.en: And then the Carthaginians send an embassy to Rome, basically to beg for mercy.
sentences.zh: 当他们到达那里时，震惊地发现罗马的这支特遣部队已经出发并抵达了西西里岛。

sentences.en: And when they arrive there, they're appalled to discover that this Roman task force has already left and is in Sicily.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，就在与迦太基隔海相望的地方。

sentences.en: So just across the sea from Carthage.
sentences.zh: 就在迦太基海的对岸。

sentences.en: And they also find Cato on absolutely top form.
sentences.zh: 他们同时也发现加图处于绝对最佳状态。

sentences.en: So he gives a kind of zinger of a speech.
sentences.zh: 于是他发表了一场极为精彩的演讲。

sentences.en: What people can't be trusted to keep their treaties?
sentences.zh: 哪些人是不能信任其会信守条约的？

sentences.en: The Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人。

sentences.en: What people are inveterate warmongers notorious for their cruelty?
sentences.zh: 哪些人是以残忍闻名、根深蒂固的好战分子？

sentences.en: The Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人。

sentences.en: What people left Italy a smouldering wasteland?
sentences.zh: 是谁将意大利变成了一片冒烟的废墟？

sentences.en: The Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人。

sentences.en: So still that harping on all the destruction that Hannibal had brought to Italy.
sentences.zh: 因此，他仍然喋喋不休地谈论着汉尼拔给意大利带来的所有破坏。

sentences.en: And when the Carthaginian envoys, you know, they beg to know, how can we make amends?
sentences.zh: 当迦太基使者前来恳求并想知道他们该如何弥补时，

sentences.en: I mean, what can we do?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们能做什么？

sentences.en: They receive this very menacingly Delphic response by satisfying the Roman people.
sentences.zh: 他们得到了一个非常具有威胁性、模棱两可的德尔斐式回答：满足罗马人民。

sentences.en: But the Senate does not specify how this satisfaction can be obtained.
sentences.zh: 但元老院并未具体说明该如何达成这种满足。

sentences.en: So let's take us to the next year, 12 months on.
sentences.zh: 让我们进入第二年，即12个月后。

sentences.en: The Romans have landed in North Africa.
sentences.zh: 罗马人已经在北非登陆。

sentences.en: They have established their base camp 30 miles northwest of Carthage.
sentences.zh: 他们在迦太基西北30英里处建立了大本营。

sentences.en: The Carthaginians sent envoys to try and negotiate with the Romans.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人派遣使者试图与罗马人谈判。

sentences.en: And what happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, they arrive at the Roman camp.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们抵达了罗马军营。

sentences.en: And as they approach, there's this kind of great deafening blast of trumpets.
sentences.zh: 当他们走近时，传来了一种震耳欲聋的巨大号角声。

sentences.en: And then they enter the camp and they are led past the massed ranks of the legions who are all drawn up and who are totally silent.
sentences.zh: 然后他们进入军营，被引导着走过排成密集的军团列队，这些军团全部列队完毕且鸦雀无声。

sentences.en: I mean, it must have been terrifying.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那一定非常可怕。

sentences.en: Ahead of them are the two consuls sat down on a podium.
sentences.zh: 在他们前方，两位执政官坐在一个高台上。

sentences.en: And the Carthaginian envoys are brought before the consuls.
sentences.zh: 迦太基使者被带到执政官面前。

sentences.en: And they start stammering, trying to make their excuses.
sentences.zh: 他们开始结结巴巴，试图寻找借口。

sentences.en: But all these excuses are dismissed.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些借口都被驳回了。

sentences.en: And then one of the consuls, Lucius Marcius Sensorinus, he informs the envoys that there will be no more negotiations until Carthage has handed over all the weapons in the city,
sentences.zh: 随后，其中一位执政官卢基乌斯·马尔基乌斯·岑索里努斯通知使者，在迦太基交出城内的所有武器之前，将不再有任何谈判，
zh_words: 卢基乌斯·马尔基乌斯·岑索

sentences.en: all the armor, all the war machines.
sentences.zh: 所有的盔甲，所有的战争机械。

sentences.en: And so the envoys go back to Carthage.
sentences.zh: 于是，使者们回到了迦太基。

sentences.en: And shortly afterwards, great wagon loads of weapons and armor come rumbling up to the
sentences.zh: 不久之后，一车车巨大的武器和盔甲隆隆地驶向罗马军营，

sentences.en: Roman camp and also in their train over 2000 catapults.
sentences.zh: 在他们的队伍中还有2000多台投石机。

sentences.en: So these are all handed over to the Romans and then the envoys come back and they stand in front of the consuls again.
sentences.zh: 这些全部移交给了罗马人，接着使者们回来再次站在执政官面前。

sentences.en: And now at last, the terms are delivered and I will quote them.
sentences.zh: 现在终于下达了条件，我将其引用如下。

sentences.en: Bear bravely the remaining commands of the Roman Senate, the envoys are told.
sentences.zh: 使者们被告知，勇敢地承受罗马元老院剩下的命令吧。

sentences.en: You must evacuate your city and surrender it to us.
sentences.zh: 你们必须撤出你们的城市并将其交给我们。

sentences.en: You will be allowed to settle where you please within the limits of your own territory, provided that it is at least 10 miles from the sea.
sentences.zh: 你们将被允许在你们自己领土范围内你们喜欢的地方安家，前提是距离大海至少10英里。

sentences.en: As for us, we are resolved to level Carthage to the ground.
sentences.zh: 至于我们，我们决心将迦太基夷为平地。

sentences.en: Imagine being the Carthaginian envoys listening to that.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，迦太基使者听到这话时的感受。

sentences.en: I mean, terrifying.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，太可怕了。

sentences.en: And of course, I mean, what can they do?
sentences.zh: 当然，我的意思是，他们能做什么？

sentences.en: There's no way that the Carthaginians can possibly accept this, you would think.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为，迦太基人绝不可能接受这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, just to emphasize for people, talked about how people are identified with their mother city.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为了向大家强调这一点，我们谈到了人们如何与他们的母城联系在一起。

sentences.en: And in a sense, to lose your mother city is to lose your identity.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，失去母城就是失去身份。

sentences.en: That city, it's not just about the history.
sentences.zh: 那座城市，不仅仅关乎历史。

sentences.en: It's also about the temples, the gods, whatever.
sentences.zh: 它还关乎神庙、神灵等等。

sentences.en: You know, you lose everything.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你失去了所有东西。

sentences.en: And of course, I mean, you know, on the economic sense, if you no longer have a port, you no longer have really have a way of kind of making a living.
sentences.zh: 当然，我的意思是，从经济角度来看，如果你不再拥有港口，你实际上也就没有了谋生的方式。

sentences.en: So as you say, I mean, it would seem impossible for the Carthaginians to accept these terMs.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，迦太基人似乎不可能接受这些条件。

sentences.en: And so it proves because when the ambassadors from the Roman camp returned to Carthage, the people of the city refused to accept it, even though they know that in effect, by doing
sentences.zh: 事实的确如此，因为当来自罗马军营的大使返回迦太基时，城里的人民拒绝接受，尽管他们知道，实际上这样做就等于

sentences.en: so, they are signing their own death warrant.
sentences.zh: 在签署他们自己的死刑令。

sentences.en: And anyone who speaks up saying, actually, I think we should accept these terMs.
sentences.zh: 任何站出来说“事实上，我认为我们应该接受这些条件”的人，

sentences.en: I mean, you know, we've got no chance of keeping the Romans at bay.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，我们没有任何机会把罗马人挡在门外。

sentences.en: They are lynched, they're stoned, whatever.
sentences.zh: 他们会被林奇私刑处死、被用石头砸死或遭遇其他不测。

sentences.en: And so there is a mass effort to try and steal Carthage for the horrors that are to come, because, of course, they've handed over their catapults, their weapons, their armor, all
sentences.zh: 因此，人们做出了巨大的努力，试图为即将到来的恐怖景象拯救迦太基，因为当然，他们已经交出了他们的投石机、武器、盔甲，所有这一切。

sentences.en: of that.
sentences.zh: 所有这些。

sentences.en: So what measures do they take?
sentences.zh: 那么他们采取了什么措施呢？

sentences.en: All the slaves in the city are freed to the degree that the Carthaginians still have arMs.
sentences.zh: 城里的所有奴隶都被解放了，只要迦太基人还有武器的话。

sentences.en: Arms are given to these slaves.
sentences.zh: 武器发给了这些奴隶。

sentences.en: People rush out to quarries outside the city and haul in stones because they're going to try and make more catapults.
sentences.zh: 人们冲到城外的采石场搬运石头，因为他们要尝试制造更多的投石机。

sentences.en: We're told all the shrines, the temples and every other public space was turned into workshops
sentences.zh: 我们得知，所有的神龛、神庙和所有其他公共空间都被变成了作坊，

sentences.en: where men and women worked day and night without pause, taking turns to eat according to a fixed schedule.
sentences.zh: 男人和女人日夜不停地工作，根据固定时间表轮流吃饭。

sentences.en: So basically, you know, equivalent of munitions factories popping up across the city in their temples.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，你知道，这就相当于军工厂在城市各处的神庙里涌现出来。

sentences.en: And in these workshops, of course, people are busy making swords, spears, shields, anything made of metal in the city is being melted down.
sentences.zh: 在这些作坊里，人们当然忙着打造剑、长矛、盾牌，城里任何金属制的东西都被熔化了。

sentences.en: And women donate their hair so that it can be used as rope for the catapults, kind of twine it.
sentences.zh: 女人们捐出她们的头发，以便用作投石机的绳索，也就是把头发编织成麻绳。

sentences.en: Hasdrubal, their general who'd lost the battle at Orescoppa and is still on death row, he's reprieved and he's given back his old command.
sentences.zh: 阿斯德鲁巴，那个在奥雷斯科帕战役中战败、目前仍在死囚牢里的将领，他被宽恕了，并被恢复了原有的指挥权。

sentences.en: And he leads out a makeshift army and prepares for a guerrilla war against the Romans.
sentences.zh: 他率领一支临时拼凑的军队，准备对罗马人发动游击战。

sentences.en: And it is war.
sentences.zh: 战争就这样爆发了。

sentences.en: For the third time, Rome and Carthage are locked in what really is this time a death struggle.
sentences.zh: 罗马和迦太基第三次陷入了一场真正意义上的生死搏斗。

sentences.en: It's not a death struggle for Rome, but it absolutely is for Carthage.
sentences.zh: 这对罗马来说不是生死搏斗，但对迦太基而言绝对是。

sentences.en: So it's the kind of war, it's a bit like, I don't know, when the Nazis invaded Poland in 1939.
sentences.zh: 所以这场战争，有点像，我不知道，就像1939年纳粹入侵波兰时那样。

sentences.en: And, you know, they had, the Germans had such a preponderance of forces, but allied sympathizers
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们有，德国人拥有压倒性的兵力，但波兰的盟友同情者

sentences.en: with Poland sort of said, oh, you know, they will have all the pluck, you know, they've got such spirit, they're fighting for their homeland, you know, the people will rise and
sentences.zh: 某种程度上说，哦，你知道，他们会拥有所有的勇气，你知道，他们充满斗志，他们是在为祖国而战，你知道，人民会奋起

sentences.en: they will see off the invaders, all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们会击退侵略者，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And actually that turned out to be complete wishful thinking because the balance of forces was such that the attacker could not but win.
sentences.zh: 而事实证明这完全是一厢情愿，因为力量对比是这样的，进攻方必然会取胜。

sentences.en: And in this case, well, actually, it's not an immediate walkover, is it, by any means?
sentences.zh: 而在这种情况下，好吧，实际上，这绝不是一场轻而易举的胜利，对吧？

sentences.en: So the Carthaginians do actually manage to hold out for much longer than the Poles do against the Nazis, as it turns out, for several years.
sentences.zh: 因此，事实证明，迦太基人确实设法坚持了比波兰人对抗纳粹长得多的时间，坚持了好几年。

sentences.en: And they're able to do this because even though the Carthaginians have had to, you know, have
sentences.zh: 他们能够做到这一点是因为，尽管迦太基人不得不，你知道，被诱骗交出了那么多的武器，但这座城市对围城的准备仍然相当充分。

sentences.en: been tricked into handing over so much of their weaponry, the city is still pretty well prepared for a siege.
sentences.zh: 所以它拥有那种宏伟的三重城墙，而这些城墙又得到了壕沟和土堤的加固。

sentences.en: So it has the kind of great triple walls, and these walls in turn are buttressed with ditches and banks.
sentences.zh: 我提到了粮仓。

sentences.zh: 因此，城内有大量的食物。

sentences.en: So they have a lot of food inside the city.
sentences.zh: 他们还建造了巨大的蓄水池来收集雨水。

sentences.en: And they've also built huge cisterns for collecting rainwater.
sentences.zh: 所以同样，水不应该成为问题。

sentences.en: So again, water shouldn't be a problem.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，罗马人向城市推进时，在一处死水湖旁扎营，当时正值夏天。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, the Romans, as they advance up to the city, they camp beside a stagnant lake and it's summer.
sentences.zh: 正如预料的那样，他们都开始，你知道，染上各种可怕的疾病。

sentences.en: And so predictably, they all start, you know, catching various horrible diseases.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，阿斯德鲁巴，你知道，他在公开战斗中被证明是个绝对的废柴。

sentences.en: And actually, Hasdrubal, who, you know, he proved an absolute dud in open combat.
sentences.zh: 当谈到游击战时，他其实相当擅长。

sentences.en: When it comes to guerrilla warfare, he's actually pretty good.
sentences.zh: 他在袭击罗马补给线、策划突围方面非常成功。

sentences.en: He's very successful at attacking Roman supply lines, masterminding sallies.
sentences.zh: 因此，在公元前149年的整整一年里，围城战一直在继续，到了公元前148年，罗马人的挫折仍在继续。

sentences.en: And so all that year, 149, the siege carries on, 148, Roman setbacks continue.
sentences.zh: 他们四处奔波，试图肃清迦太基城外的迦太基据点。

sentences.en: They are going around trying to mop up Carthaginian strongholds beyond Carthage.
sentences.zh: 但这些据点也能够坚守。

sentences.en: But these two are able to hold out.
sentences.zh: 同样，城墙内发起了突击，他们烧毁了罗马的攻城器械等等。

sentences.en: And again, sallies are launched out from the walls and they burn Roman siege engines and so on.
sentences.zh: 接着在公元前148年，马萨尼萨，你知道，那位老将，那位伟大的人物，那个曾经是迦太基盟友后来又变成他们大敌的人，

sentences.en: And then in 148, Masanissa, you know, the old war horse, the great, the man who had once been a Carthaginian ally and then become their great enemy.
sentences.zh: 在91岁的高龄去世了。

sentences.en: He dies at the fabulous age of 91.
sentences.zh: 这或许曾给迦太基人带来希望，也许，你知道，这个他们根深蒂固的敌人已经离去了。

sentences.en: And that might have offered hope to the Carthaginians, perhaps, you know, that this kind of inveterate enemy of theirs has gone.
sentences.zh: 随后巴尔干半岛传来了消息，出现了马其顿王位的觊觎者。

sentences.en: And then there comes news from the Balkans that a pretender to the Macedonian throne has emerged.
sentences.zh: 人们还记得马其顿王国曾被划分成这四个行政区。

sentences.en: So people remember that the kingdom of Macedon had been divided up into these four cantons.
sentences.zh: 出现了一个王位觊觎者，他想要重新统一这些行政区并让自己成为国王。

sentences.en: A pretender has emerged and he wants to reunite these cantons and make himself king.
sentences.zh: 他击败了一支罗马军队，并向迦太基人传话：你们愿意结盟吗？

sentences.en: And he defeats a Roman army and sends messages to the Carthaginians saying, will you enter into an alliance?
sentences.zh: 当然，迦太基人回答：愿意。

sentences.en: And of course, the Carthaginians say, yes.
sentences.zh: 所以他们突然确实有了一个盟友。

sentences.en: So suddenly they do have an ally.
sentences.zh: 现在，罗马人，你知道，他们并没有沮丧。

sentences.en: Now, the Romans, you know, they're not despondent.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然完全期望获得胜利。

sentences.en: They're still fully expecting to win.
sentences.zh: 但我认为某种程度上的恐慌正在滋生。

sentences.en: But I think there's a certain sense of alarm developing.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始四处寻找救世主，一个有资格挺身而出并证明自己是英雄的人。

sentences.en: And so they start to look around for a saviour, someone qualified to step into the breach and prove himself a hero.
sentences.zh: 当然，实际上只有一个候选人。

sentences.en: And there is, of course, really only the one candidate.
sentences.zh: 所以显而易见的人选，我猜，就是大西庇阿的养孙，也就是我们已经讨论过的人，小西庇阿。

sentences.en: So the obvious person, I guess, the adoptive grandson of Scipio Africanus, it's the person we've already talked about, Scipio Aemilianus.
sentences.zh: 这不仅因为他拥有正确的血统或正确的遗传。

sentences.en: And it's not just that he has got the right bloodline or the right heredity.
sentences.zh: 他有经验，不是吗？

sentences.en: He has experience, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他已经与迦太基人战斗过了。

sentences.en: He has already fought the Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 他确实打过。

sentences.en: He has.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是一个非常非常优秀的士兵。

sentences.en: I mean, he's a very, very good soldier.
sentences.zh: 他曾在奥雷斯科帕担任观察员，当时马萨尼萨击败了迦太基人。

sentences.en: So he'd been an observer at Orescoppa where Masanissa had defeated the Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 因此他近距离观察过迦太基总司令阿斯德鲁巴。

sentences.en: And so he had seen Hasdrubal, the Carthaginian commander in chief, up close.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他了解他的脾气秉性。

sentences.en: You know, he knew what made him tick.
sentences.zh: 在过去的两年里，他一直在迦太基城墙前服役，在那里他基本上是唯一一位获得任何声誉的高级军官。

sentences.en: And then for the past two years, he'd been serving before the walls of Carthage itself, where he was basically the only senior officer to have emerged with any credit at all.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他经历了一场非常棒的战争。

sentences.en: I mean, he'd had a very good war.
sentences.zh: 唯一的缺点是他还在30多岁。

sentences.en: The only drawback is that he's still in his 30s.
sentences.zh: 人们会记得担任执政官的最低年龄是40岁。

sentences.en: And people will remember that the minimum age to serve as consul is 40.
sentences.zh: 为了小西庇阿，这一规定曾在遭到罗马保守派反对的情况下被破例豁免。

sentences.en: That had been waived for Scipio Africanus against the opposition of Roman conservatives.
sentences.zh: 但民众并不在意。

sentences.en: But the people hadn't cared.
sentences.zh: 他们强行推行了此事。

sentences.en: They'd forced it through.
sentences.zh: 这一次也发生了同样的事情。

sentences.en: And the same thing happens this time.
sentences.zh: 民众，我引用原话，“宣布他是他的父亲马其顿征服者埃米利乌斯·保卢斯以及西庇阿家族唯一当之无愧的继承人”。

sentences.en: The people, and I quote, declared that he was the only worthy successor of his father,
sentences.zh: 因此，元老院认识到民意的力量，或许，你知道，自己也感到有些绝望，同意放弃这一禁令并表示，

sentences.en: Aemilius Paulus, the conqueror of Macedon, and of the Scipios.
sentences.zh: 是的，小西庇阿可以竞选执政官，并且他顺利当选了。

sentences.en: And so the Senate, recognising the force of public opinion, perhaps, you know, just a little desperate themselves, agree to waive the prohibition and say,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，甚至连保守主义的绝对代言人加图，

sentences.en: yeah, Scipio can run for consul and he's duly elected.
sentences.zh: 连加图也对小西庇阿表示了认可。

sentences.en: And the intriguing thing is that even the absolute spokesman for conservatism,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他真的是胜任这份工作的合适人选。

sentences.en: Cato, even Cato gives Scipio Aemilianus the nod.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们终于迎来了故事的最后一章。

sentences.en: I mean, he really is the right man for the job.
sentences.zh: 也就是迦太基之围、布匿战争的结束，以及这座伟大的古代城市本身的终结。

sentences.en: So now at last, we come to the final chapter in the story.
sentences.zh: 罗马人将所有的希望都寄托在了小西庇阿身上。

sentences.en: So the siege of Carthage, the end of the Punic Wars, and indeed the end of this great ancient city itself.
sentences.zh: 当他在公元前146年作为执政官抵达非洲时，汤姆，他拥有他的前任们所缺乏的活力、朝气和雄心。

sentences.en: So the Romans have put all their hopes in Scipio Aemilianus.
sentences.zh: 他完全不负元老院对他的厚望。

sentences.en: And when he arrives in Africa as consul in 146, Tom, he has the vigour and the dynamism and the ambition that his predecessors have lacked.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he more than bears out the hope that the Senate had in him.
sentences.zh: 而曾与小西庇阿发生过冲突的阿斯德鲁巴，我的意思是，他非常尊重他的声誉。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 因此，他没有继续他的游击战，而是将所有部队撤回迦太基城内并在那里固守。

sentences.en: And Hasdrubal, who has clashed with Scipio Aemilianus before, I mean, he's very respectful of his reputation.
sentences.zh: 但这样做，当然只是正中小西庇阿的下怀，因为现在所有的迦太基军队都被困在了这座大城市里。

sentences.en: And so he, rather than continuing with his guerrilla war, he withdraws all his troops inside Carthage and hunkers down there.
sentences.zh: 小西庇阿知道，如果他能完全包围这座城市，彻底封锁它，切断所有的食物供应，

sentences.en: But this, of course, is only to play into Scipio Aemilianus's hands, because now all the Carthaginian forces are trapped inside the great city.
sentences.zh: 那么从长远来看，他将能够通过饥饿迫使这座城市投降。

sentences.en: And Aemilianus knows that if he can only invest the city completely, completely surround it, cut off all supplies of food,
sentences.zh: 于是他命令部下在港口入口处开始建造一道巨大的防波堤，这在迦太基人看来是一个不可能完成的工程项目。

sentences.en: then he will be able in the long run to starve the city into submission.
sentences.zh: 但小西庇阿不仅是一名优秀的士兵，也是一名极好的工程师，并且能够成功将其建成。

sentences.en: And so he orders his men to start constructing a massive mole across the entrance of the harbour, which to the Carthaginian seems an impossible engineering project.
sentences.zh: 最终这道防波堤建成了。

sentences.en: But Scipio Aemilianus is a very good engineer as well as a very good soldier and is able to pull it off.
sentences.zh: 通往港口的通道现已被封锁，食物运进迦太基的可能已不复存在。

sentences.en: And so this mole ends up being constructed.
sentences.zh: 因此小西庇阿知道他现在可以高枕无忧地等待了。

sentences.en: Access to the harbour is now blocked off and there is no possibility of food coming into Carthage.
sentences.zh: 随着每一天的流逝，绞索都会收紧。

sentences.en: And so Scipio Aemilianus knows that he can now sit back and wait.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人怎么样了？

sentences.en: And with each day that passes, the noose will tighten.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这绞索正在收紧。

sentences.en: And what about the Carthaginians?
sentences.zh: 他们在做什么？

sentences.en: Well, this noose is tightening.
sentences.zh: 占位符

sentences.en: What are they doing?
sentences.zh: 占位符

sentences.en: Well, Carthage has always been run by a Senate in that sense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从这个意义上说，迦太基一直是由元老院管理的。

sentences.en: It's always had a kind of civilian government.
sentences.zh: 它一直拥有一种某种形式的文官政府。

sentences.en: But Hasdrubal, he feels that the only way that Carthage survive is if he institutes a military dictatorship.
sentences.zh: 但哈斯德鲁巴认为，迦太基要想生存下去，唯一的办法就是建立军事独裁统治。

sentences.en: And so this is what he does.
sentences.zh: 于是他便这么做了。

sentences.en: You know, he's got all the soldiers at his back.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他背后有所有的士兵支持。

sentences.en: There's no one to stop him.
sentences.zh: 没有人能阻止他。

sentences.en: That, of course, he is able to commandeer all the food supplies within the city and ensure that his men are well fed, even while everyone else starts to starve.
sentences.zh: 当然，这样一来，他就能征用城内的所有粮食储备，确保自己的人吃饱肚子，而其他人则开始挨饿。

sentences.en: And the corpses of those who no longer have access to food begin to litter the streets of the dying city.
sentences.zh: 那些不再能获得食物的人的尸体开始布满这座垂死城市的街道。

sentences.en: And Hasdrubal is anxious that this experience of starvation on the part of the vast majority of the public
sentences.zh: 哈斯德鲁巴十分担心，广大民众经历的这种饥荒

sentences.en: may result in civic unrest may lead to pressure on him to open negotiations with the Romans.
sentences.zh: 可能会导致公民骚乱，可能会给他施加压力，迫使他与罗马人开启谈判。

sentences.en: And he's not prepared to do that.
sentences.zh: 而他对此毫无准备。

sentences.en: So he takes Roman legionaries who've been captured in the fighting and he leads them up onto the walls of Carthage.
sentences.zh: 于是他将在战斗中俘获的罗马军团士兵带到了迦太基的城墙上。

sentences.en: And there, where the Romans far below can see what is being done to their comrades, they're tortured to death and their bodies are dumped into the Roman positions.
sentences.zh: 在那里，远处的罗马人能看到他们的战友正遭受怎样的虐待，他们被折磨至死，尸体被扔进了罗马人的阵地中。

sentences.en: So that, of course, makes sure that there will be no negotiations.
sentences.zh: 当然，这确保了双方绝无谈判的可能。

sentences.en: And Scipio Aemilianus is waiting for the morale in the city to hit rock bottom, for people really to start dying, for disease to spread.
sentences.zh: 小西庇阿正等待着城中士气降至谷底，等待人们真正开始死亡，等待瘟疫蔓延。

sentences.en: And then when that moment comes, he strikes and he takes the Carthaginians completely by surprise.
sentences.zh: 然后在那个时刻到来时，他发起进攻，彻底打了个迦太基人一个措手不及。

sentences.en: And his assault, it's not over the walls, it's through the harbours from the mole.
sentences.zh: 他的进攻不是翻越城墙，而是通过防波堤从港口攻入。

sentences.en: That mole is a kind of launch pad.
sentences.zh: 那条防波堤就像是一个发射台。

sentences.en: And so the Romans are able to, it's an amphibious attack.
sentences.zh: 因此罗马人能够发动一场两栖登陆作战。

sentences.en: They go through the outer harbour into that inner harbour that the Carthaginians have just been built.
sentences.zh: 他们穿过外港，进入迦太基人刚刚修建的那个内港。

sentences.en: And from there, there is easy access to the great marketplace in the centre of the city.
sentences.zh: 从那里可以轻松通往市中心的大集市。

sentences.en: And once the Romans have breached the harbour defences, they pour into this marketplace and they essentially make it the base for the sack of the city that is now going to happen.
sentences.zh: 一旦罗马人突破了港口防御，他们便涌入这个集市，并将其基本上作为即将展开的毁城之战的基地。

sentences.en: First of all, they strip this great temple that is standing there of all its gold, pile that gold up.
sentences.zh: 首先，他们剥离了耸立在那里的这座宏伟大殿的所有黄金，把黄金堆积起来。

sentences.en: And then they start literally disassembling the city brick by brick.
sentences.zh: 然后他们开始字面意义上一砖一瓦地拆解这座城市。

sentences.en: So what they do, there are kind of very tight, narrow streets fanning off from the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 他们的做法是，集市向外延伸出一些非常狭窄的街道。

sentences.en: And there are blocks of housing that reach up six storeys.
sentences.zh: 那里有高达六层的住宅楼。

sentences.en: And these are about the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 这些建筑都围绕着集市。

sentences.en: And the houses that are adjacent to the marketplace, soldiers go in, they clear all the opposition from all the enemy from the each of the stories of these houses.
sentences.zh: 对于紧邻集市的房屋，士兵们闯进去，肃清这些房屋每一层的所有抵抗和敌人。

sentences.en: And then once the houses have been cleared, they take planks up to the top storey and they lay them out across the kind of narrow streets below.
sentences.zh: 一旦房屋被清空，他们就会把木板搬到顶层，横搭在下方狭窄的街道上。

sentences.en: And from there, they can pass into the next block of houses and they do the same.
sentences.zh: 从那里他们可以进入下一栋住宅楼，然后重复同样的操作。

sentences.en: And the process just goes on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 这个过程就这样没完没了地进行下去。

sentences.en: And once the houses have been cleared and the soldiers have gone from the one block to the next, they then set the houses on fire.
sentences.zh: 一旦房屋被清空，士兵们从一栋楼推进到下一栋，他们就会放火烧毁这些房屋。

sentences.en: And you get masonry, you get beams, you get the corpses of the slain, you get old men, women, children who might have taken shelter inside these houses.
sentences.zh: 于是砖石、横梁、阵亡者的尸体，以及可能在这些房屋内部避难的老人、妇女和儿童，

sentences.en: They all come crashing down into the streets.
sentences.zh: 全都轰然坠入街道。

sentences.en: And we have a horrific description of what this was like.
sentences.zh: 我们有关于当时惨状的可怕描述。

sentences.en: So a kind of hideous, grotesque image.
sentences.zh: 这真是一种可怕而怪异的景象。

sentences.en: Do you know what it reminds me of?
sentences.zh: 你知道这让我想起了什么吗？

sentences.en: It reminds me of the siege of Tenochtitlan that we talked about in the fall of the Aztecs.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起了我们在讲阿兹特克帝国灭亡时谈到的特诺奇蒂特兰围城战。

sentences.en: The Spanish fighting house by house, destroying the houses to stop the Aztecs from using them as kind of refuges.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人逐屋巷战，摧毁房屋以阻止阿兹特克人将其作为避难所。

sentences.en: I mean, it's very, very similar, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这非常非常相似，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's this Stalingrad style battle.
sentences.zh: 这就是斯大林格勒式的战役。

sentences.en: I mean, it's possible that there would have been Spaniards.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当时的战争中很可能有一些西班牙人

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 读过这些历史记载。

sentences.en: In the war who had read these very accounts.
sentences.zh: 我也是这么想的。

sentences.en: I was thinking that.
sentences.zh: 对，他们很多人都受过古典教育。

sentences.en: Yeah, they had classical education, a lot of these people.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对这一切都很了解。

sentences.en: So they would have known about all this.
sentences.zh: 而这，迦太基的毁灭，是一座宏伟、著名且美丽的首都毁灭的典型代表。

sentences.en: And this, the destruction of Carthage is the archetype of the destruction of a great and famous and beautiful capital.
sentences.zh: 清剿的过程持续了六天。

sentences.en: And the process of clearance goes on for six days.
sentences.zh: 到了第七天，幸存的大多数迦太基人投降了。

sentences.en: And on the seventh day, the vast mass of the Carthaginians who remained alive surrendered.
sentences.zh: 现在唯一的抵抗来自哈斯德鲁巴和900名罗马逃兵，他们坚守在最高处的堡垒上，也就是迦太基版的卫城。

sentences.en: And the only resistance now is from Hasdrubal and 900 Roman deserters who held out on the kind of the topmost fort, the Carthaginian equivalent of an Acropolis.
sentences.zh: 但最终，他也只能选择投降，他被带到小西庇阿面前，在罗马指挥官脚下匍匐求饶。

sentences.en: But in time, he too is brought to surrender and he's brought before Scipio Aemilianus and grovels before the feet of the Roman commander.
sentences.zh: 而一直和他在一起的妻子对他的这种行为极其鄙视。

sentences.en: And his wife is, who'd been with him, is utterly contemptuous of this.
sentences.zh: 她拿起一把匕首。

sentences.en: And she takes a dagger.
sentences.zh: 割断了他们两个儿子的喉咙，并把儿子的尸体扔进附近熊熊燃烧的火焰中。

sentences.en: She slits the throats of their two sons and she throws the corpses of her sons into a fire that is blazing nearby.
sentences.zh: 然后她自己也纵身跃入火海。

sentences.en: And then she hurls herself into the flames as well.
sentences.zh: 非常有狄多女王的风范。

sentences.en: Very Dido.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有点悲哀的是，女性往往只有在自杀时才会出现在这个系列中。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a bit sad that women tend only to appear in the series when they're killing themselves.
sentences.zh: 这就是古代社会的常态。

sentences.en: That's antiquity for you.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 那么哈斯德鲁巴和那些逃兵怎么处理？

sentences.en: So what happens to Hasdrubal and what happens to the deserters?
sentences.zh: 哈斯德鲁巴被饶了一命，被带回罗马，在小西庇阿的凯旋式上游行。

sentences.en: So Hasdrubal is spared and taken back to Rome where he walks in Scipio Aemilianus' triumph.
sentences.zh: 然后他被允许在罗马郊外的一座农场定居。

sentences.en: And then he's allowed to settle in a farm outside Rome.
sentences.zh: 所以他活了下来。

sentences.en: So he survives.
sentences.zh: 至于罗马逃兵，当然是被极其残忍地处死了。

sentences.en: The Roman deserters, of course, are put horribly to death.
sentences.zh: 投降的迦太基人则全部沦为奴隶。

sentences.en: The Carthaginians who surrendered, they are all enslaved.
sentences.zh: 大约有五万人。

sentences.en: About 50,000 of them.
sentences.zh: 他们被带出城。

sentences.en: They're led out.
sentences.zh: 男人、女人、孩子，全都成为了奴隶。

sentences.en: Men, women, children, all become slaves.
sentences.zh: 这座城市的各种宝藏被系统性地洗劫一空。

sentences.en: The city is systematically stripped of all its treasures.
sentences.zh: 迦太基诸神的庙宇没有受到丝毫尊重。

sentences.en: No respect is shown the temples of the Carthaginian gods.
sentences.zh: 它们被彻底摧毁了。

sentences.en: They are demolished.
sentences.zh: 迦太基有着丰富而悠久的文学传统。

sentences.en: Carthage had a rich and venerable literary tradition.
sentences.zh: 所有的图书馆都被搬空并送给了努米底亚人，而后者似乎很快就把它们给弄丢了。

sentences.en: All the libraries are emptied and given to the Numidians, who promptly seem to have lost them.
sentences.zh: 罗马人确实保留了一部28卷的农学著作，并将其翻译成了拉丁语，因为他们显然在想，我们要接管这些土地。

sentences.en: The Romans do keep one 28-volume treatise on agriculture, which they have translated into Latin, because obviously they're thinking, well, we want to take over these lands.
sentences.zh: 这是如何让田野丰饶的指南。

sentences.en: And this is the guide to how to, you know, how to make the fields flourish.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会保留它。

sentences.en: So we'll keep that.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，布匿文学的所有财富都烟消云散了。

sentences.en: But otherwise, all the wealth of Punic literature is gone.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一无所有。

sentences.en: So we have nothing.
sentences.zh: 我们没有由迦太基人撰写的历史。

sentences.en: We have no histories written by the Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 因此，正如这些历史故事中经常出现的那样，无论是刚果的比利时人，还是别的什么，

sentences.en: And so, as so often, you know, in these stories, whether it's the Belgians in the Congo or whatever,
sentences.zh: 或者实际上是大平原上的美国人，我们只有一种视角。

sentences.en: or indeed the, you know, the Americans in the Great Plains, we only have one side.
sentences.zh: 我们只有罗马人的视角。

sentences.en: We only have the Roman side.
sentences.zh: 迦太基陷落的消息传到罗马，随后元老院向西庇阿

sentences.en: The news of Carthage's fall is sent to Rome, and the Senate then sent back instructions to Scipio
sentences.zh: 埃米利安努斯下达指令，要求将城中残存的一切彻底夷为平地，并诅咒任何未来试图在那里定居的人。

sentences.en: Aemilianus that what remained of the city was to be razed to the ground, and that a curse was to be laid on anyone who in the future might try to settle there.
sentences.zh: 因此迦太基将被荒废，任由杂草丛生。

sentences.en: So Carthage is to be left abandoned to weeds.
sentences.zh: 但神奇的是。

sentences.en: But here's an amazing thing.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有在废墟上撒盐。

sentences.en: They don't sow the ruins with salt.
sentences.zh: 每个人都以为他们这么做了，但其实并没有。

sentences.en: Everyone thinks they did that, and they didn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他们没这么做。

sentences.en: No, they don't.
sentences.zh: 这是出版于20世纪20年代的《剑桥古代史》中的一个隐喻性修辞。

sentences.en: It was a metaphorical flourish in the Cambridge ancient history, which came out in the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 从那以后它就像野火一样传开了。

sentences.en: And it's just spread like wildfire ever since.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，在任何古代史料中都完全没有关于这种行为的记载。

sentences.en: But that did, you know, there's no reference to that happening in any of the ancient sources at all.
sentences.zh: 不过，他们撒不撒盐其实也没区别，因为这座非常著名、非常古老、非常美丽的城市的毁灭，

sentences.en: But, you know, they might as well have sowed the fields with salt, because the signal that the destruction of this very famous, very ancient, very beautiful city,
sentences.zh: 向世界发出的信号是毋庸置疑的，那就是罗马人再也不允许任何对手、任何一丝叛逆的存在。

sentences.en: the signal sent to the world was unmistakable, that the Romans are no longer prepared to brook any rival, any hint of disobedience.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，这个信息再次得到了强有力的印证。

sentences.en: And that is a message that is rammed home a few months later.
sentences.zh: 大家可能还记得，马其顿发生了一场叛乱，出现了一个马其顿王位的觊觎者。

sentences.en: So people may remember that, you know, there's this uprising in Macedon, this pretender to the Macedonian throne has emerged.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他没撑多久。

sentences.en: I mean, he does not last long.
sentences.zh: 他被击溃了。

sentences.en: He gets crushed.
sentences.zh: 接着希腊也爆发了一场叛乱，罗马人同样以极其残暴的手段进行了镇压。

sentences.en: And there's then a kind of, there's an uprising in Greece, and the Romans deal with that very brutally as well.
sentences.zh: 对这场叛乱的镇压最终导致了第二座著名、古老且美丽城市的毁灭，这就是希腊科林斯的消亡。

sentences.en: And the suppression of that uprising culminates in the annihilation of a second famous, ancient and beautiful city, and that is the destruction of Corinth in Greece.
sentences.zh: 它扼守着连接伯罗奔尼撒半岛与希腊北部的地峡。

sentences.en: Commanding the isthmus that joins the Peloponnese to northern Greece.
sentences.zh: 我认为公元前146年的任何地中海人，

sentences.en: And I think that anyone in the Mediterranean in 146 BC,
sentences.zh: 在目睹同年迦太基和科林斯的毁灭时，都会清楚地意识到一个时代的降临：罗马的势力如此庞大，

sentences.en: contemplating the destruction in the same year of Carthage and of Corinth, are well aware that an era has dawned in which Rome is so preponderant
sentences.zh: 以至于实际上地中海再也没有任何人拥有真正的独立地位了。

sentences.en: that effectively no one in the Mediterranean has any real independence left at all.
sentences.zh: 而且，用不了区区一个世纪，整个地中海就会变成罗马的内湖。

sentences.en: And, you know, within a century, the whole of the Mediterranean will become a Roman lake.
sentences.zh: 但是，关于罗马是如何崛起达到这种霸权地位的，这对地中海的人民意味着什么，对罗马人自己又意味着什么，

sentences.en: But the story of how Rome rises to that position of preponderance, what it means for people in the Mediterranean and what it means for the Romans themselves,
sentences.zh: 这些，我们改天再聊。

sentences.en: I mean, that is a story for another day.
sentences.zh: 但我只是觉得在结束这个系列时——我们总共做了三个系列，我们在最初的那个系列的第一期就引用了一段源自波利比乌斯回忆录的文字。

sentences.en: But I just thought to end this series, we've done three series in all, and we began the very first series with a passage that derives from Polybius' recollections.
sentences.zh: 波利比乌斯曾陪同小西庇阿参加了围城战并亲眼见证了这一切。

sentences.en: Polybius had accompanied Scipio Aemilianus to the siege and had witnessed it for himself.
sentences.zh: 所以我就以宣读这段文字来作为结语。

sentences.en: So I'll just finish by reading this passage.
sentences.zh: 据说小西庇阿看着迦太基在烈火中化为灰烬，其灭亡已成定局，他凝视着这座在死前痛苦挣扎的城市，为他的敌人公开落泪。

sentences.en: It is said that Scipio Aemilianus, as Carthage was going up in flames, its annihilation almost complete, gazed at the city in its death throes and openly wept for his enemies.
sentences.zh: 他久久伫立，陷入沉思，

sentences.en: He stood wrapped in thought for a long time,
sentences.zh: 思索着每一座城市、每一个民族、每一个帝国，正如凡人一样，最终都必然会迎来它们的末日。

sentences.en: pondering how every city, every people, every empire must, as men do, meet with their doom in the end.
sentences.zh: 因为特洛伊曾是一座骄傲而繁荣的城市，亚述、米底和波斯帝国曾各自称霸世界，

sentences.en: For such had been the fate of Troy, once a proud and flourishing city, and of the empires of Assyria, Media and Persia, each in their own day the greatest in the world,
sentences.zh: 而马其顿不久前还曾光芒万丈，这就是它们的命运。

sentences.en: and of Macedon, which only recently had blazed with such a brilliance.
sentences.zh: 随后，无论是刻意为之还是情不自禁地引用，

sentences.en: And then, either deliberately or because he could not help quoting them,
sentences.zh: 西庇阿吟诵了两行荷马史诗。

sentences.en: Scipio spoke two lines of Homer.
sentences.zh: 神圣的特洛伊终将灭亡的那一天终会到来，普里阿摩斯及其子民也将被尽数诛杀。

sentences.en: A day will come when sacred Troy shall perish, and Priam and his people all be slain.
sentences.zh: 当波利比乌斯凭借作为西庇阿希腊文学导师所享有的直言不讳的特权问他这些话是什么意思时，

sentences.en: And when Polybius, speaking to him with the freedom he was granted as Scipio's tutor in Greek literature, asked him what he meant by these words.
sentences.zh: 据说西庇阿没有丝毫掩饰其含义，

sentences.en: It is said that without any attempt to veil his meaning,
sentences.zh: 而是直接暗示了自己的祖国。

sentences.en: Scipio made reference to his own country.
sentences.zh: 因为当他沉思于所有必朽之物都终将倾覆时，他内心深处也恐惧着罗马终有一日也会走向毁灭。

sentences.en: For when he pondered how all things that are mortal must fall, he dreaded how Rome too would fall.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 好吧，非常感谢你，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, thank you very much, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这是一个沉重的警告，也为我们周一即将开播的下一个系列《历史其余部分》（The Rest is History）做了极好的铺垫。

sentences.en: That's a salutary warning, and indeed one that sets up beautifully our next series on The Rest is History, which will be starting on Monday.
sentences.zh: 那个系列讲的是印加帝国灭亡的故事，这是世界历史上持续时间最长、规模最大的绵延帝国之一，

sentences.en: And that series is the tale of the fall of the Incas, one of the longest and largest contiguous empires in world history
sentences.zh: 却在弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗及其征服者的手中轰然崩塌。

sentences.en: that came crashing down at the hands of Francisco Pizarro and his conquistadors.
sentences.zh: 因此，在周一，“历史其余部分”俱乐部的会员将获得这个宏大系列的所有六集内容。

sentences.en: So on Monday, members of The Rest is History Club will get all six episodes in that mighty series.
sentences.zh: 如果你想加入他们，如果你想与西班牙人一起深入库斯科和卡哈马卡的街头、亚马逊的丛林，并攀登安第斯山脉的山峰，

sentences.en: And if you want to join them, if you want to plunge into the streets of Cusco and Cajamarca and the jungles of the Amazon and scale the peaks of the Andes with the Spaniards,
sentences.zh: 那么你只需前往 TheRestIsHistory.com 注册，周一就能收看全部六集节目。

sentences.en: then you merely have to head to TheRestIsHistory.com to sign up, and you'll get all six episodes on Monday.
sentences.zh: 但现在，汤姆，能用三个宏大的季节来讲述这段史诗般的历史，真是一项了不起的成就。

sentences.en: But for now, Tom, what an amazing effort to cover that epic story in three mighty seasons.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 这就是迦太基的故事。

sentences.en: And that was Carthage.
sentences.zh: 大家再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye, everybody.
sentences.zh: 万岁。

sentences.zh: 再见。
